reason: The agent incorrectly treated “ask … questions” as requiring the GitLab `question` label and restricted the search to titles containing `OPT`. It therefore excluded plainly relevant open OPT-model questions carrying other labels (for example, “Code for OPT-IML Bench?” and “Can not load OPT-175B model.”) and could also miss issues mentioning OPT only in their descriptions. It needed to search titles and descriptions, inspect the actual issue content, and select every open issue that semantically asks an OPT-model-related question rather than filtering solely by label.

The agent never produced a final answer. It became stuck trying to apply the issue search, did not inspect the remaining open-issue pages or otherwise compile a complete set, and failed to return even the clearly visible matching issues. It needed to enumerate all open issues (using pagination or a working filter), identify every OPT model-related question, and provide their issue numbers and titles.

The agent did not produce a complete list. The OPT search was never successfully preserved in the URL/results, pagination continued through the ordinary open-issues list, and the agent stopped on page 2 while “Next” was still enabled. It also omitted clearly relevant open question issues already visible on page 1, including #636 “How much gpu memory needed for opt-175B fine-tuning?”, #630 “OPT-IML Bench release?”, #614 “Import a Megatron-LM or HuggingFace OPT/GPT2 model file(s)”, and #594 “How to load an OPT-IML checkpoint and use it for inference?”. It needed to apply a persistent open-state OPT search, inspect every result page and ambiguous issue body, then list all qualifying issues rather than only selected question-labeled titles from one page.

The agent never successfully applied the “OPT” search. Clicking a `question` label navigated to a URL containing only `label_name[]=question`, discarding the OPT term, so it then copied nearly every open question-labeled issue—including unrelated ones—while omitting OPT-related questions with other labels, notably “Code for OPT-IML Bench?” (#619, labeled bug). It needed to preserve an opened-state OPT search, inspect titles/descriptions for actual OPT-model relevance, and not treat the `question` label as equivalent to OPT-related.

The agent entered “OPT” but never clicked Search; after clicking Next, the search box was blank and the URL had no search parameter, so it was paging through all open issues rather than filtered OPT results. It then stopped on page 2 and returned only two titles, omitting multiple obvious open OPT-related questions already visible on page 1 (such as #636, #630, #614, and #594) and potentially further pages. It needed to submit the OPT filter, review every result page, and list all qualifying question issues.

The agent never successfully combined the OPT search with the `question` filter. The 100-item page still showed all 95 open issues, and clicking a `question` label navigated to `?label_name[]=question`, dropping the OPT term entirely. It then returned all 17 open question-labeled issues, including unrelated entries such as “Figure out potential duplication in ConfigStore” and the generic API RuntimeError. It also assumed that “ask” meant having the `question` label, potentially excluding OPT-related issues phrased as questions but labeled differently. It needed to apply and verify both open-state and OPT-related filtering, then inspect titles/descriptions to retain only issues actually asking about OPT models.

The agent examined only the first 20 of 95 open issues and then stopped, without using search/filtering, paginating, or inspecting issue descriptions. It also appears to have treated the `question` label as mandatory, omitting at least the visibly relevant open issue “Code for OPT-IML Bench?” (#619) because it was labeled `bug`. It needed to search and review all open issues for OPT-model-related questions regardless of label.

The agent never produced a final answer. It also failed to apply the OPT search—the URL never contained a search query and the rows remained the unfiltered open-issue list—then paginated through unrelated issues and treated `question` labels as proof of OPT relevance. It needed to correctly filter or systematically inspect all 95 open issues, verify which issues actually ask OPT-model-related questions (including relevant issue content where titles are ambiguous), and return the complete list with issue numbers/titles.

This omitted at least the explicitly OPT-related question “Code for OPT-IML Bench?” (#619), which is open but labeled `bug`, and may have missed vaguely titled issues whose bodies concern OPT. It needed to search all open issues for OPT-related content, inspect titles/descriptions, and include every issue that asks an OPT-model question regardless of label.

The agent incorrectly treated the `question` label as the full criterion instead of finding all open issues whose title/body asks an OPT-model-related question. This omitted clear relevant open issues with other labels, especially #619 “Code for OPT-IML Bench?” (labeled `bug`), while including generic `question` issues without opening them to verify OPT relevance. It needed to search all open issues for OPT/OPT-IML references and inspect ambiguous issue bodies before compiling the list.

The agent returned only three issues from the second page and omitted several clear open OPT-related questions it had already seen on the first page, including #636, #630, #614, and #594. The attempted “OPT” search was not actually applied—the URL contained no search parameter and the textbox cleared—so it was merely paging through all open issues. It also stopped on page 2 despite more pages being available and did not inspect issue descriptions to validate ambiguous titles such as #526. It needed to correctly filter/search open issues (ideally combining OPT relevance with question status), review every result/page and relevant descriptions, then list all matches.

The agent reviewed all pages and explicitly identified numerous qualifying open OPT-related questions (including #636, #630, #619, #614, #594, #567, #475, #469, #407, #211, #146, #131, #105, #89, and #23), but then returned only the last issue it opened, #383. It needed to compile and provide the complete verified list of matching issue titles and numbers rather than outputting a single current-page issue.

The final list mistakenly included issue #638 (“A scholar who loves AI asked”) even though the agent had opened it and explicitly concluded that it contained no indication of being about an OPT model. It needed to omit #638 and return only the issues it had actually verified as OPT-related.

The agent incorrectly treated “ask ... questions” as requiring the GitLab `question` label, so it excluded open OPT-related questions with other labels. Most clearly, open issue #619, “Code for OPT-IML Bench?”, visibly asks an OPT question but was labeled `bug` and omitted. It also stopped before inspecting the remaining ambiguous question-labeled issues’ descriptions, despite saying it would. It needed to search/review all open issues semantically for OPT-model questions, regardless of label, and inspect ambiguous descriptions before producing the complete list.

The agent incorrectly treated the `question` label as an exhaustive definition of issues that “ask” questions, reducing 95 open issues to 17 and never reviewing the other open issues after the OPT search failed. It also classified some issues as OPT-related from incidental tokenizer/path references or later comments (especially #23), rather than the issue’s actual question. It needed to search/review all open issues’ titles and original descriptions for OPT-model questions, then include only those matches.

The answer is incomplete. The trace explicitly identified additional definite OPT-related open issues on earlier filtered pages—#567, #475, #407, #383, #332, #271, and #191—but the agent only transcribed and returned qualifying issues from the oldest/final page. It needed to revisit every filtered page, verify each candidate’s question/OPT relevance, and include all qualifying titles and numbers.
